title: Quantization lineage anchoring and revert strategy
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Goal: produce a reproducible, auditable lineage model and operational revert strategy for quantization artifacts (FP8/INT8) that ties calibration inputs, deterministic calibration state, and deployed binaries together with a cryptographically verifiable anchor. This ticket defines: 1) a compact provenance manifest format and deterministic serialization rules, 2) a dual-hash anchoring approach (artifact binary hash + calibration-dataset fingerprint), 3) an append-only ledger/anchor store and signing workflow, and 4) safe rollback mechanics including migration scripts and compatibility mappings for model checkpoints and runtime kernels.
acceptance_criteria: Provenance manifest JSON schema v1 documented and reviewed
Calibration-run deterministic serializer implemented and produces stable hashes for the same inputs across CI runs
Dual-hash anchoring stored in the quant-registry and visible in Console UI (hash links to artifact and calibration dataset)
Signed manifest flow integrated with KMS and keys can be rotated without breaking verification
Rollback playbook that can revert a deployed quantized model to a prior anchored manifest with automated validation tests
End-to-end integration test in CI that creates a calibration run, publishes manifest, verifies signature, deploys model, and executes revert
implementation_notes: Use deterministic protobuf-to-json serialization rules: stable key ordering, canonical float formatting, and explicit field presence for defaults

Manifest fields: artifact_hash (sha256 hex), calibration_fingerprint (sha256 of dataset + seed + preprocessing), runtime_compatibility_tags (list), quant_profile_id, calibration_metadata_url, signer_key_id, created_at
Anchor store: implement minimal append-only ledger backed by existing quant-registry DB with content-addressable index and immutable commit ids (CID style)
Signing: integrate with existing KMS connector used by releases; signatures must be verifiable by Console and by private deployments using public keys
Rollback: create a revert orchestration that can perform a canary rollback to previous manifest and run the calibration smoke suite before full traffic migration
Compatibility mapping: provide a mapping table for FP8<->INT8 equivalent profiles and list known runtime kernel constraints
Edge case: handle deleted calibration datasets by keeping an immutable snapshot reference or storing dataset fingerprint plus digest-of-commit-id
Storage constraints: do not duplicate large datasets; manifest should reference dataset snapshot URLs or dataset-catalog ids
test_plan: Unit tests for canonical manifest serializer and hash determinism
Integration test: create calibration job -> publish manifest -> verify signature -> deploy -> run regression prompts -> revert to previous manifest -> verify outputs match golden tolerance
Fuzz test: vary float tolerances and confirm fingerprint changes appropriately
Security test: rotate signer keys in staging and verify old manifests still verify via key rotation metadata
Performance test: publish 1000 manifests and verify anchor store query latency under load
rollout_plan: Phase 1 (staging): implement serializer + anchor API; run internal calibration jobs and surface manifests in Console; collect feedback
Phase 2 (canary): enable signed manifest verification on a single Dedicated pool and require manifest signature for model promote flows
Phase 3 (gradual): require manifest anchoring for all public quant artifacts and add rollback hooks to deployment pipeline
Phase 4 (audit): export ledger for compliance audits and add retention/archival policy
